equity_bridge.item: NCI (51.24%) share of PTFI net debt added back
equity_bridge.note: ESTIMATE. PTFI carries the ~$3.2B downstream (Manyar smelter) facility and ~$0.8B of cash (Q2 2026 10-Q / Analysis.json), net ~$2.4B; 51.24% = ~$1.2B. Consolidated net debt of 5,306 deducts 100% of PTFI's debt while the flows are attributable-only, so without this the minority's share of PTFI's debt would be charged to FCX shareholders (~$0.83/share).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle volume pipeline (~1-1.5%/yr: Grasberg full ramp, Bagdad, Safford/Lone Star, leach, Kucing Liar) plus ~2% price inflation. The historical CAGRs are NOT used as a forward anchor: for a copper/gold miner they describe where in the price cycle the endpoints fell (FY2020 COVID trough, FY2022 $4.03 peak, FY2025 Grasberg outage), not the business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 10.5% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 30.1% (>30% divergence) and revenue 3yr 3.7% vs 5yr 12.8%: all endpoint artefacts of the FY2020 trough (EPS $0.41) and the FY2025 Q4 Grasberg outage. Equity CAGRs are on TOTAL equity including NCI (the only continuous series in the CSV); parent-only equity grew 16,693 -> 18,899 FY2023-25 (6.4%/yr).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC incl. equity-award tax withholding; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 940, FY2021 5,473, FY2022 1,520, FY2023 296, FY2024 2,208, FY2025 972. Reported FCF: 1,056 / 5,600 / 1,670 / 455 / 2,352 / 1,116. SBC is ~0.5% of revenue so the owner and reported CAGRs are within 1pp; the divergence between them is not the story here -- the NCI leakage is (see inputs.nci_treatment). FY2022-25 capex of $3.5-4.8B/yr carried the $3.7B Manyar smelter and Grasberg underground development, depressing FCF versus the FY2021 peak.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle. Grasberg Block Cave completes its phased restart on the revised schedule (90k tpd by Q2 2027), restoring the gold-rich, lowest-cost production that was ~70% of pre-incident output; FY2027 copper sales rise ~20% and gold ~50% as guided. Copper and gold do not stay at the 2026 records: copper glides from ~$5.90 to a $5.00/lb mid-cycle by FY2028 (above the FY2011-25 range, consistent with the higher incentive price for new supply) and gold from ~$4,300 to $3,500/oz. Consolidated EBITDA margin settles at 40% pre-SBC. The Indonesian state (51.24% of PTFI plus ~42% effective tax/royalty take) and Peru's minorities continue to absorb ~two-thirds of EBIT, so FCX shareholders keep ~33 cents of each EBIT dollar and bear ~69% of the capex. Volume grows ~1-1.5%/yr from Bagdad, Safford/Lone Star, leach innovation and Kucing Liar, funded from cash flow; El Abra is not sanctioned. Attributable owner FCF runs ~$1.6-3.0B/yr, in line with FCX's FY2019-25 attributable history of $0.5-4B.
scenario_narratives.bull: Structural deficit. AI/data-centre power, grid electrification and EVs keep refined copper in deficit through the decade and the price holds ~$5.75/lb with gold ~$4,200 -- essentially today's deck sustained. Grasberg ramps on time and Kucing Liar, El Abra (sanctioned 2027), Bagdad and the leach programme lift volume ~3%/yr into the mid-2030s; margins reach 45% and North America's larger 100%-owned share of EBIT cuts the leakage rate to 64%. Section 232 tariffs on refined copper (15% 2027 / 30% 2028 under review) add a US price premium. Attributable owner FCF climbs from ~$2.3B to ~$4.4B by FY2036.
scenario_narratives.bear: Downcycle plus execution. A China/global slowdown of the 2015-16 or 2019 kind takes copper to $4.00/lb and gold to $2,800 by FY2028; the wet-drawpoint problems that already cut the 2026 ramp target from 100k to 60k tpd recur and push the full Grasberg ramp into late 2027. Margins fall to ~30%, the high-cost North American mines earn little so Grasberg (51% minority, heavily taxed) dominates EBIT and leakage rises to 72%. Growth capex is deferred to sustaining levels as in 2016 and 2020. Attributable owner FCF is ~$1.0-1.2B/yr and the terminal multiple is capped at 12x. Indonesian fiscal renegotiation ahead of the 2041 extension (a further 12% stake transfer is already mandated) is the unmodelled tail below this case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on attributable flows. Three things drive the gap between this valuation and the price. (1) Price deck: the market is capitalising ~$6+ copper and ~$4,400 gold; the base case glides to $5.00/$3,500, still above the fifteen-year range. (2) Leakage: FCX owns 48.76% of its crown-jewel asset and Indonesia's tax/royalty take on PTFI is ~42%, so roughly two-thirds of every EBIT dollar goes to the Indonesian state, MIND ID and Peru's minorities -- consolidated EBITDA multiples flatter FCX badly. (3) Capex: reserve replacement and the Grasberg/Kucing Liar development keep attributable capex ~3.4pp of revenue above attributable D&A in perpetuity. Attributable owner FCF has ranged $0.5-4B/yr over FY2019-25; a $104B market cap needs $5-6B sustained. The bull case (near-spot deck held for ten years, full pipeline built) still lands well below the price, which says the market is paying for scarcity/optionality value in the ore bodies and a spot-forever assumption rather than for owner cash flow at any mid-cycle deck.
key_risks_to_valuation: Price deck: each $0.50/lb of sustained copper is ~$2.1B of consolidated revenue and ~$0.6-0.7B of attributable owner FCF (~$6-8/share at the terminal multiple); the model's mid-cycle $5.00 is a judgment, and a structural shift to $6+ is the bull case, not a mid-cycle one

NCI leakage calibration: the combined tax + minority rate (67% base) is calibrated to FY2023-25 reported attributable income; each 1pp is ~$0.10B/yr of attributable FCF (~$1/share). The 12% further PTFI stake transfer to Indonesia by 2041 sits beyond the horizon but would lift leakage further

Attributable D&A/capex shares (65%/69% of consolidated) are estimates from segment disclosures, not reported figures; the equity_bridge add-back for the minority's share of PTFI net debt (~$1.2B) is likewise an estimate

Grasberg execution: a further ramp slip, a repeat geotechnical incident, or a fiscal renegotiation ahead of the 2041 extension is the bear tail; Grasberg is ~half of reserves and the highest-margin output

Terminal multiple: Gordon at 10%/2.5% (13.7x) binds below the 15x cap; a spot-based EV/EBITDA framework, which is how the street prices copper majors, implies far higher values than an owner-FCF Gordon value can reach

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (Friday regular close); 52-week range 36.05-80.24
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 831259) via research/FCX/Reports/FCX_Metrics.csv and core_metrics (FY2006-Q2 2026). NCI (NetIncomeLossAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest, MinorityInterest), attributable net income (NetIncomeLoss), diluted shares, dividends to common and to NCI, cash taxes paid, LongTermDebt and tax-withholding on equity awards pulled directly from companyfacts on 2026-09-28 because core_metrics has no NCI, diluted-share or dividend-paid columns. Balance sheet and share count: Q2 2026 10-Q (2026-06-30).
data_sources.qualitative: research/FCX/Reports/FCX_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): Q2 2026 guidance (FY2026 copper ~3.1B lbs, gold ~650k oz, moly ~93M lbs, unit net cash cost ~$1.90/lb, OCF ~$8.3B at $6.00 Cu; H2 copper >+20% and gold >+65% vs H1; FY2027 copper >+20%, gold >+50%), Grasberg restart schedule, PTFI ownership, buyback and dividend programme.

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2025 10-K: ShareBasedCompensation $121M (cash-flow add-back) + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $23M. FCX publishes no combined equity-award figure, so the two lines are summed (method 1a). H1 2026: $103M + $44M.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares Q2 2026 10-Q: 1,443M (basic 1,443M; dilution <1M). Held FLAT at 1,444M because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks ($107M FY2025, $203M H1 2026 under the $5B authorisation, ~$2.9B remaining) fund the flat count and are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Total debt 9,386 = XBRL LongTermDebt at 2026-06-30 (8,166 non-current + 1,220 current portion), less cash and equivalents 4,080. NOTE: core_metrics/Metrics.csv total_debt of 10,606 double-counts the 1,220 current portion (same pattern FY2025 9,845 vs XBRL 9,379; Q1 2026 9,914 vs 9,414) and is NOT used. The 5,306 consolidated figure ties to FCX's own 'net debt ~$2.1B excluding $3.2B PTFI downstream (smelter) debt'. Consolidated net debt includes PTFI's debt at 100% while the flows are attributable-only; the minority's share of PTFI's net debt is added back in equity_bridge so NCI is charged exactly once.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.2-1.4 for a diversified copper major -> cost of equity ~10.5-11%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% at ~10% debt weight -> WACC ~10%. Held at 10.0% in ALL scenarios: commodity-price and Grasberg execution risk are carried in the scenario dispersion and weights, not stacked in the discount rate (adaptations f: charge risk once). Raw CAPM on a 5y beta of ~1.7 would say ~12% -- that would be charging the cyclicality twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP; operating lease liabilities are immaterial (<$0.4B against $9.4B of debt) and lease cost is already inside operating costs/EBITDA. Treatment (B) by default: no lease liabilities in net debt, no separate lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: ATTRIBUTABLE-ONLY FLOWS (adaptations c). FCX consolidates PT Freeport Indonesia (owns 48.76%; MIND ID/Inalum 51.24%) and Cerro Verde (53.56%). NCI took $1,903M / $2,510M / $1,948M of consolidated net income of $3,751M / $4,399M / $4,152M in FY2023-25, i.e. 51% / 57% / 47%; H1 2026 $913M of $2,778M (33%, Grasberg half-down). Implementation: (1) cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED cash-tax + NCI leakage rate on EBIT, calibrated so modelled attributable NOPAT ties to reported attributable net income + after-tax interest: FY2023 ~70%, FY2024 ~72%, FY2025 ~66%, H1 2026 ~55% (annualised). Forward base 67% at full Grasberg and $5/lb copper (North America's 100%-owned share of EBIT is higher at $5 than at FY2024's $4.21); bull 64%; bear 72%. (2) da_pct_path and capex_pct_path are FCX's ATTRIBUTABLE share of consolidated D&A (~65%: Indonesia ~50% of D&A x 48.76%, Cerro Verde ~20% x 53.56%, rest 100%) and capex (~69%: Indonesia ~50% of capex, Cerro Verde ~12%), so the minority bears its share of Grasberg/Kucing Liar development and the Manyar smelter rather than FCX shareholders being charged 100% of consolidated capex against a 33% share of EBIT. Consolidated equivalents: D&A ~8.5%->8.0% of revenue, capex ~16% (FY2027) -> 12.5% (mature). (3) NCI's share of PTFI net debt added back in equity_bridge. FY0 tie: FY2026E revenue 28.8B x 39.5% EBITDA - SBC - attributable D&A 5.5% = EBIT ~9.6B x (1-0.57) = ~4.1B attributable NOPAT = ~$2.87/share vs H1 2026 actual EPS $1.29 and a guidance-implied stronger H2 (~$2.9-3.0 FY2026E).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component-built, MID-CYCLE, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (NCI, risk charged once). Routed via dcf-methods: FCX is an operating company (copper/gold/molybdenum miner), highly cyclical, with a 51% minority in its largest asset. Reference treatment: BSL.AX / FMG.AX / CMM.AX / IGO.AX mid-cycle owner-FCF builds. FY0 = FY2026E (fiscal year ends 31-Dec, three months out): revenue 28,800 = H1 2026 actual 13,263 + H2E ~15,540 built from Q2 2026 guidance (H2 copper sales >20% above H1, gold >65% above H1, moly flat, ~Q2 realised prices ~$5.75/lb Cu, ~$4,300/oz Au). Y1 = FY2027. PRICE DECK (the axis that matters): FY2026 realised ~$5.75-6.00/lb Cu and ~$4,300-4,500/oz Au are at/near record highs. Base mid-cycle: copper glides to $5.00/lb and gold to $3,500/oz by FY2028 (nominal, then +2%/yr), which is above the FY2011-2025 range and reflects the raised incentive-price consensus ($4.50-5.50) rather than history; bull holds near-spot $5.75 Cu / $4,200 Au; bear reverts to $4.00 Cu / $2,800 Au (a 2015-16/2019-style downcycle, not a crash). VOLUMES: Grasberg Block Cave ramp per guidance (60k tpd H2 2026 -> 90k tpd Q2 2027): FY2027 copper +20%, gold +50%; FY2028 Block 1S/1C adds a few %; thereafter ~1-1.5%/yr from Bagdad, Safford/Lone Star, leach and Kucing Liar, with El Abra only in the bull. EBITDA MARGIN is pre-SBC consolidated (the engine deducts SBC separately): FY2024 actual 36.2% at $4.21/$2,400 with full Grasberg; FY2021 45.4% at $4.33/$1,800 before the 2022-25 cost inflation; H1 2026 39.8% at ~$5.7/$4,300 with Grasberg half-down. Segment cross-check at $5.00/$3,500 with 2028 costs: Indonesia EBITDA ~$8.5B, North America ~$2.0B, South America ~$2.8B, moly ~$0.3B, corporate -$0.6B = ~$12.9B on ~$31B = ~41%; base uses 40% mature. INTEREST INCOME not stripped: FCX is a net-debt company (cash 4.1B vs debt 9.4B), so its ~$150-200M/yr interest income stays in the flows and net debt is deducted at face. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventories exceed payables, so wc_capture is -5% (growth consumes cash; declines release it). SBC is ~0.5% of revenue -- house and street bases nearly coincide; band_position is reported but the band is only ~$1/share wide. TERMINAL: Gordon at 10%/2.5% is 13.7x FCF, below the 15x cap (12x in bear), so Gordon binds in base/bull. WHAT THE PRICE IMPLIES: at $72 the market cap is ~$104B against attributable owner FCF that has ranged $0.5-4B/yr over FY2019-25 (consolidated FCF less NCI distributions); the price needs ~$5-6B/yr of sustained attributable FCF, i.e. roughly today's $6+ copper and $4,400 gold in perpetuity plus the full growth pipeline -- a spot-forever deck, not a mid-cycle one. That is the finding, not an error: an owner-FCF model on a cyclical at a price peak with ~50% NCI and ~40% government take will sit far below a spot-based EV/EBITDA multiple.

bear.growth_note: Downcycle deck: China/global slowdown takes copper to $4.75 in FY2027 and $4.00 by FY2028, gold to $2,800; Grasberg ramp slips another two quarters (FY2027 Cu volume +10% not +20%, Au +30% not +50%); growth projects deferred; 2% nominal growth thereafter.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: FY2023 was 36.7% at $3.85/$1,950 on a pre-inflation cost base; FY2019 was 17% at $2.73. 29-30% at $4.00/$2,800 with 2028 costs.
bear.da_pct_note: Attributable; D&A dollars are roughly fixed so the ratio rises on lower revenue.
bear.capex_pct_note: Attributable; growth capex cut to sustaining plus committed Grasberg development, as FCX did in 2016 and 2020.
bear.cash_tax_rate_note: Higher leakage: at $4.00 the high-cost North American mines earn little while low-cost Grasberg (51% minority, ~42% Indonesian take) dominates EBIT.

base.growth_note: FY2027: Grasberg volumes (Cu +20%, Au +50% per guidance) net of price normalisation (Cu $5.9 -> $5.25, Au $4,300 -> $3,800). FY2028: +3% Cu / +10% Au volume (Blocks 1S/1C) net of the glide to $5.00 / $3,500. FY2029-31 +3.5% (2% inflation + Bagdad/leach/Kucing Liar volume), fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC consolidated. FY2027 ramp year (wet drawpoints, restart costs, $1.50/lb unit cost target not yet reached). Mature 40% at $5.00 Cu / $3,500 Au with 2028 costs; segment build gives ~41%, FY2024 actual was 36.2% at $4.21/$2,400.
base.da_pct_note: FCX-ATTRIBUTABLE D&A (~65% of consolidated 8.5% -> 8.0%). See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.capex_pct_note: FCX-ATTRIBUTABLE capex (~69% of consolidated 16% FY2027 -> 15% -> 14% -> 13% -> 12.5% mature). Consolidated FY2027 ~$4.9B: Grasberg UG development, Kucing Liar, Bagdad expansion, sustaining ~$2.3B. Mature attributable 8.6% vs attributable D&A 5.2% leaves ~3.4pp (~$1.3B) of growth/reserve-replacement capex funding the 2.5% terminal growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: COMBINED cash tax + NCI leakage on EBIT (attributable-D&A basis). Calibrated FY2023 ~70%, FY2024 ~72%, FY2025 ~66%, H1 2026 ~55%. FY2027 65% while Grasberg (the most heavily taxed and 51% minority-owned unit) is still ramping; 67% at full Grasberg and $5 copper.

bull.growth_note: Structural-deficit deck: copper holds ~$5.75 and gold ~$4,200 (near spot) as AI/grid/EV demand outruns mine supply; Grasberg ramps on schedule; El Abra sulfide ($7.5B, 51% FCX) sanctioned 2027 and Kucing Liar, Bagdad, Safford/Lone Star and leach add ~3%/yr volume through the mid-2030s; Section 232 refined-copper tariff lifts US realisations.
bull.capex_pct_note: Attributable; higher and longer than base because El Abra and the full brownfield pipeline are built.
bull.cash_tax_rate_note: Lower leakage: at $5.75 the 100%-owned North American mines carry a larger share of EBIT.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: copper and gold are at or near record highs, so mean reversion is at least as likely as persistence; the Grasberg ramp has already missed its own revised target once; and a single underground complex in Indonesia is a single point of failure for ~half the reserves. Bull cut to 25%: it needs three independent things to hold at once -- near-spot metal prices in perpetuity, an on-schedule ramp, and a sanctioned growth pipeline (El Abra) that is not yet approved.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
